criteria: The active Sys4AI depot root shall expose one coherent project-local Curator process through its governance, charter, configuration, owner entry points and ontology, using the root's actual project identity and current operating policy.

The ontology shall represent the supported Curator process and its meaningful functions, including policy inspection, scoped review, owner-routed update and correction, exact retry/recovery, Task pause/resume, selected dispatch, session catch-up and bounded log access.

Curator ontology knowledge shall connect the process to project identity, governing skills and roles, Task lifecycle/current ownership, memory, ontology and maintenance obligations, with typed relationships and inspectable source provenance.

Reusable source collections and the registered Sys4AI Template shall contain the complete Curator project and ontology capability needed for destination specialization through the supported initializer.
Supported Sys4AI new-project creation shall deliver Curator project wiring and its functional ontology integration together as part of the same successful initialization workflow.

First-time Sys4AI preparation of a selected existing project shall supply the same integrated Curator process and ontology functionality while preserving the destination's established identity, authored content and explicit configuration choices.

Sys4AI shall provide a supported explicitly selected adoption or refresh route that completes Curator project and ontology integration for previously initialized projects, including those with an earlier Curator installation that lacks ontology integration.

Integration setup and adoption shall preserve authored ontology and memory, Task history, project identity, licensing, custom packages, unrelated roles and explicit opt-outs, with exact change boundaries and recoverable operations.

Curator project behavior and ontology representation shall consistently describe bounded session-start/return collection, subsequent current-owner evaluation and separately authorized execution, preserving the configured session-only operating mode.
The root's pending Curator catch-up obligations identified by the health report shall receive current-owner disposition based on fresh bounded evidence and current source/ownership checks.

The reported staged response under the cancelled historical Curator Task shall be investigated through the Task owner, with any lifecycle or native-write-ownership mismatch reconciled before a supported recovery or cleanup disposition.
The root health follow-up shall establish actual local browser behavior for the selected on-demand ontology workbench and report its operating state accurately without requiring an always-on service.
The integration and report follow-up shall preserve the working root memory retrieval, ontology core/backend behavior and their independent data, configuration and authority boundaries.

Final integration reporting shall cover root, reusable sources, neutral Template and each supported initialization/adoption route, relating every requirement and health finding to current evidence and explicit limits.
